title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from this page and its neighbours). S is a base scheme. G is a form of GL(2)_S with determinant G → G_m. SG is the corresponding form of SL(2), with centre μ_2. T_ρ and T_σ are (±) tori 'en l'air', i.e. abstract tori not yet embedded in G, with epimorphisms δ_ρ: T_ρ → G_m and δ_σ: T_σ → G_m. One later chooses embeddings T_ρ, T_σ → G.

The group scheme M°_{ρ,σ} was first built as a semidirect product. Earlier pages established:
- G⁺_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG is a normal subgroup;
- Γ°_{ρ,σ} = M°/G⁺ ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ;
- R°_{ρ,σ} is commutative and surjects onto Γ°;
- R° is central in M°.

The page finishes the proof of (75): R° ∩ G⁺ = Ker(R° → Γ°) = μ_2. It adds a second argument. Since R° is central in M°, the intersection R° ∩ G⁺ lies in the centre of G⁺ ≅ SG, which is μ_2. So the intersection is contained in μ_2, and the equality already shown in (74) forces it to be all of μ_2.

Remark: a simpler, intrinsic description of M°.
- (77) Define R° by diagram (74). It is a central extension 1 → μ_2 → R° → T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ → 1, with inclusion j'.
- (78) Define M° as the central amalgamated product (central product) M° = (R° × SG)/μ_2, where μ_2 is embedded anti-diagonally by ε ↦ (j'(ε), j''(ε⁻¹)) and j'': μ_2 → SG is the inclusion of the centre.
- (79) This parallels the well-known presentation G = (G_m × SG)/μ_2, with ε ↦ (ε, j''(ε⁻¹)).
- (80) The canonical map R° → G_m from (74) (a 'square root of the determinant' type map) gives a morphism of extensions from (78) to (79). Passing to quotients, this yields Θ°: M° → G (next page).

Purpose: to describe M° purely in terms of T_ρ, T_σ, the δ's and the form G. The next page then turns to sections M°(0) of the extension of Γ° by SG, which 'will play an essential role'. Plausibly (not stated on the page), ρ and σ are the order-3 and order-2 generators of the modular group, and T_ρ, T_σ are the tori attached to the elliptic points (Z[ζ_3], Z[i]). The whole is a group-scheme model for the 'lacets' (braid/loop) relations in Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. (79) must be read as exact in the fppf topology: G_m × SL_2 → GL_2 is not surjective on points over a non-closed field or ring, and μ_2 is not étale over Z at 2. Grothendieck's notation is compatible with this reading.

The alternative argument for (75) uses that the centre of the form SG is exactly μ_2 (true for forms of SL_2 as group schemes). It only gives the inclusion ⊂ μ_2; equality relies on the earlier computation in (74), as the text says.

ideas.what: Intersection of a central subgroup with a normal SL_2-form lies in the centre μ_2 of SL_2
ideas.modern_name: centre of SL_2 as a group scheme
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general structure of reductive group schemes)

ideas.what: Presentation of M° as the central product (R° × SG)/μ_2, where R° is a μ_2-central extension of T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ
ideas.modern_name: central product / pushout of central extensions; GL_2 = (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2

ideas.what: Morphism of central-product presentations induced by R° → G_m, giving Θ°: M° → G
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of central products (isogeny to GL_2)

missed.claim: The construction is a group-scheme ('en l'air', over a general base S) model built from two tori T_ρ, T_σ with norm-like maps to G_m and a form of GL_2. It apparently serves to encode the order-2 and order-3 generators of the modular group in Grothendieck's study of the lacets equation. The role of the sections M°(0), announced on the next page, is not developed here. As far as I know, no published work treats such group-scheme models of the elliptic points of the Teichmüller tower in this form.
missed.quote: et on définit M°_{ρ,σ} comme somme amalgamée centrale (78) 1 → μ_2 → R°_{ρ,σ} × G⁺_{ρ,σ} → M°_{ρ,σ} → 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This may be relevant to arithmetic and motivic models of the modular-group relations (GT, elliptic Grothendieck–Teichmüller). That relevance can only be judged with the surrounding pages; the content of this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine algebraic-group manipulations: a central product presentation analogous to GL_2 = (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2. The only interest is the unpublished context, a group-scheme framework for the ρ, σ (lacets) relations, which this page alone does not substantively reveal.
transcription_corrections: Page number '515' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination; '426' at the bottom is the archive page.
'par la diagramme (74)' should read 'par le diagramme (74)'.
'par l'égalité' likely refers to the equality in (75)/(74): 'mais est en fait égal par l'égalité (75)'.

Before (79) the line reads roughly 'Notons qu'on a une description bien connue de G en termes de SG comme' ('comme' appears to start the next line; 'description' is an insertion over a crossed-out word).
The crossed-out start of (78) is '(78) M_{ρ,σ}', abandoned before the final version.
